answer: Sequential delay proofs: each epoch an agent must compute a verifiable delay function seeded by the fresh epoch nonce, about 10^9 chained squarings that take roughly an hour on the fastest core and cannot be split across machines. Like a glacier, it moves at one pace however much hardware is piled on, while peers verify the proof in milliseconds. A farm of 1,000 fake seats needs 1,000 top cores busy all epoch, near $1 of rent each per day, yet each clone sips only a thin share of the nectar, so the attack never reaches its summit of profit.
